exposure: maternal dietary patterns (derived via factor analysis)
Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet adherence
cohort: The study included 3143 participants from the PIN (Pregnancy, Infection, and Nutrition) study.
finding: Specific unhealthy maternal dietary patterns characterized by high consumption of collard greens, red meats, processed meats, fried foods, and whole milk were associated with increased odds of preterm birth, while greater adherence to the DASH diet was associated with decreased odds.
gest_age: The study assessed dietary intake at 26-29 weeks of gestation and focused on preterm birth, which is defined by gestational age.
